blind_spots.blind_spot: A 500+ megapixel, 75 fps panoramic stream has no path off the platform in a contested link — and no stated on-board reduction strategy
blind_spots.operator_reality: On a Group 2/3 UAS or a tactically responsive space vehicle, the downlink is measured in single-digit Mbps and drops for minutes at a time. Their own numbers imply tens of gigabits per second of raw sensor output. Whatever reaches the analyst is whatever survived a link they never describe — the same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case where the contested environment could carry one frame every five seconds.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The Hydra lineage came out of cinematography and VR capture, where the camera writes to local storage over a fat cable and nobody has to budget bandwidth. The SBIR abstracts still describe performance in cinematic terms (72-megapixel video, RGBD on the fly) rather than in bits per second delivered to a consumer.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: for cinematic or VR imaging capture. With the addition of a dual sensing modality, such as LIDAR or event sensors, the Medusa configuration can also support a variety of applications including photogrammetry or mapping, security or surveillance, or object tracking, generating a RGBD data stream on the fly

blind_spots.blind_spot: A situational-awareness sensor for counter-UAS and perimeter security that never mentions ATAK/TAK or any government back-end it must feed
blind_spots.operator_reality: Counter-UAS detections that don't land as a CoT message on the ATAK end-user device the E-5 is already carrying are detections nobody acts on. The buying command will ask which C2 system consumes the track and who owns that integration; 'integrates rapidly' is not an answer to a program office. Every dollar of the sensor's value is downstream of an integration they have not scoped.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Circle sells the optic, not the kill chain — their differentiation is analog parallax elimination at the lens, so their engineering conversation stops at pixel integrity. Nothing in ~1012 words of their own language names a downstream consumer of the imagery beyond generic 'autonomy stacks'.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: our systems integrate rapidly and perform reliably at the edge—whether mounted on drones, embedded in ISR platforms, or deployed in immersive simulations

blind_spots.blind_spot: SWaP-C for a multi-aperture polygonal lens array is never quantified, and 'no gimbal required' is treated as the whole platform-integration story
blind_spots.operator_reality: A compound-eye head with a plurality of adjacent sensors plus the compute to mosaic them in real time is a mass, power, and thermal problem on any small aerial platform — it displaces battery, which displaces endurance, which is the number the unit actually cares about. Inside an engine as a borescope it is a heat and clearance problem. No mass, watt, or endurance-delta figure appears anywhere in their own language while pixel counts appear repeatedly.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their patent story is about eliminating parallax in analog rather than in software, so the internal metric of success is image quality and latency, not watts per useful frame. Removing the gimbal reads to them as the SWaP answer, so the sensor-plus-compute budget never gets stated.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: capable of real-time spherical imaging that is stitch-less, parallax-free, and doesn't require a gimbal to operate on aerial platforms

opener_hook: Your AFWERX borescope purchase order FA864925P0516 is at 100% of its $1.7M ceiling, and the Medusa abstract targets 500+ MP at 75 fps — a rate no tactical downlink I've worked has ever carried off the platform.
what_they_do: Builds multi-aperture 360-degree cameras whose polygonal lenses eliminate parallax optically, so panoramic video needs no software stitching, aimed at drones, ISR platforms, counter-UAS perimeter security, and aircraft inspection.
